chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from one who informed him, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
"No one performs tawaf between these two stones, al-Safa and al-Marwah, except that he is released from the state of ihram, except for the one bringing the offering (saiq al-hady)."
As for the concession regarding the postponement of tawaf for the Mufrid, that has been narrated.

key_terms.سَائِقُ الْهَدْيِ: the one bringing the sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: Does performing tawaf between Safa and Marwah release a pilgrim from ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal mechanism of exiting ihram through the sa'i between Safa and Marwah, distinguishing the general pilgrim from the 'saiq al-hady' who must maintain ihram until the sacrifice. Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to highlight the specific exception for those accompanying their sacrificial animal, while also referencing the concession for the Mufrid regarding the timing of tawaf, reflecting the nuanced juristic discussions on Hajj rituals in Shia fiqh.
